lens.2: Conventionally: “I see a mango and want it.” Ultimately: cittas, mental factors, an eye-base and a visible form, with no owner behind them.
lens.3: Six kinds of citta in one process: adverting #28, seeing #20, receiving #25, investigating #26, determining #29, then javanas of #3, greed with joy, without wrong view, unprompted.
lens.4: Seeing carries only the 7 universals. Each javana carries 18: the 7, the 6 occasionals, the 4 unwholesome universals and greed. Conceit may join as a 19th.
lens.5: Eye-sensitivity is kamma-born; the mango's colour is temperature-born. The javanas make mind-born matter: perhaps a smile, or a hand reaching out.
lens.7: A very great object: seeing at moment 5, the wanting in javanas 9–15, registration at 16–17, then back to the life-continuum.
lens.8: Eye-base: prenascence and support. Colour: object. Adverting: proximity. Greed: root. Each javana: repetition. Volition: kamma.
lens.9: Contact → feeling → craving. This is the second connection, where present results turn into present causes.
lens.10: Unwholesome kamma. By time: J1 may ripen in this life, J7 in the next, J2–6 in any later life. Repeated often, it becomes habitual kamma.
lens.11: If kamma like this produces rebirth, it leads to a woeful plane; within a human life it ripens as unwelcome sights and sounds.
lens.13: Mindfulness notes “wanting”. Insight sees it arise and pass. Sensual desire is weakened at once-return and ended at non-return.
